ppi_focus: Radiator support and front crossmember corrosion: confirm whether it is surface-only or pitting through.
Electric water pump and thermostat: scan for coolant pump fault codes, check the pump part date, and inspect the expansion tank and hoses for brittleness or seepage.
Oil-filter-housing gasket, valve-cover gasket and oil-pan gasket seepage, viewed from below.
Paint-meter the whole car to confirm repaint is limited to the bumper cover and trunk.
Convertible top operation, seals and drain channels; trunk floor and footwells for moisture.
Clutch engagement, slave/master hydraulics and the dual-mass flywheel noise at idle.
Front control-arm (thrust) bushings and rear subframe/control-arm corrosion and bushings.
Full module scan and confirmation of recall completion; brake fluid condition.
Tire DOT dates, and curb-damaged wheels for bends or runout.
what_would_change_verdict: Up: a clean third-party PPI before the close, plus close-up photos showing the radiator-support corrosion is superficial.
Up: Carfax or receipts showing water pump, thermostat or OFHG service, or a clean scan with confirmed recall completion.
Down: confirmed structural corrosion on the radiator support or frame-rail ends, or evidence of trunk or footwell water ingress.
Down: active oil leaks or water pump fault codes found at inspection, or the dealer declining a PPI with this little time left.
evidence.mission_note: A six-speed, naturally aspirated M Sport 128i squarely matches the enthusiast-bridge brief and should resell easily within 6-24 months. The open questions are inspection access in the two days left and undocumented cooling service, not fit.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes identity well: the VIN decodes to a 2013 128i convertible, and the Carfax snapshot shows one owner, 21 service records and a clean DC title. The six-speed manual and M Sport equipment are visible in the photos. Observed issues are cosmetic and disclosed: repainted front bumper cover and trunk, curb-marked wheels, and a January 2026 'very minor' roof damage entry, which the seller explains as a top tear with a Robbins replacement invoice. A commenter's claim of pitting and rust on the radiator support is disputed by the seller; those photos were not examined here and the point stays open. The underside photo shows surface corrosion typical of a Northeast car, with no visible rot. Both model-critical items rest on seller words: the dealer has no water pump information, and 'no leaks' comes from their own inspection, with no photos of the OFHG or oil-pan areas. Recall completion and tire date codes are also unestablished. The $3,000 bid is not indicative of where this no-reserve car will settle.
evidence.next_action: Contact the dealer today to request a third-party PPI in Marlboro, NY before the October 20 close, together with the full Carfax PDF and close-up photos of the radiator support and oil-filter-housing area.
